newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to maintain ethanol subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to maintain ethanol subsidies.

text.p: The Brazilian government has decided to delay the end to subsidies and the lifting of price controls for ethanol, due to have taken place on January 1, a senior commodities official said.
Pedro Cabral, head of the sugar and alcohol department in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, told reporters he did not know how long the subsidies would remain in place.

Cabral said Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles had asked President Fernando Henrique Cardoso for an extra year to allow the alcohol industry to adjust to an environment of free competition with other fuels.
"How long subsidies continue now depends on the president," he said.
Earlier this year, the government announced as part of a general liberalization of fuel prices the end to subsidies and price controls from the beginning of next year.
But ethanol distillers, accustomed to being bankrolled by the government under the two-decade-old Pro-Alcohol Campaign, said they needed more time to adjust.
